t: Minimum Sum of Values by Dividing Array — DP over AND States
o: Partition nums into m contiguous blocks whose ANDs equal the targets. Key fact: fixing a right endpoint, the set of distinct AND values of subarrays ending there has size O(log(max)) — each new element either keeps or clears bits, so the AND chain collapses quickly. DP state: (index, number of closed segments, current partial AND) with the minimum sum of block-end values. Transition: extend the open block (AND shrinks), or close it when the AND equals the next target (cost adds the last element). n ≤ 1e4, m ≤ 10, and few distinct ANDs per position make this feasible.
k: Suffix-AND values from any position collapse to O(log V) distinct values.
DP over (position, segments closed, current AND) with dictionary-valued states.

a.i: dp[j] maps current partial AND → minimal cost so far with j segments closed. For each new element, either fold it into the open block or, if the folded AND hits andValues[j], close the block and pay the element as the block's last value.
s: Per element, rebuild states: extend (v & x) within level j; if equal to andValues[j], move cost + x to level j+1 with fresh AND.
Answer: min of dp[m] if non-empty, else -1.
a.t: O(n · m · D) where D ≤ ~17 distinct AND states per level — effectively O(n·m·log V)
a.sp: O(m · D) for the DP dictionaries

a.n: Approach 2: Memoized recursion on (i, j, current AND)
a.i: Top-down variant: f(i, j, v) = min cost to finish from index i with j targets done and open-block AND v. Same state space, easier to derive but recursion overhead and memo keying make the iterative dict version cleaner in practice.
s: Option 1: recurse to i+1 with v & nums[i].
Option 2 (if v & nums[i] == andValues[j]): pay nums[i], recurse with fresh AND and j+1.
Base: i == n valid iff j == m and block closed.
a.t: Same O(n·m·D) state space; recursion adds constant overhead

w: The 'few distinct suffix ANDs' lemma is the whole problem — without it the state space is unbounded. Pitfalls: representing 'fresh block' AND as all-ones (use ~0 / -1), and remembering a block must be non-empty (closing consumes the current element). Follow-up: prove the O(log V) bound via vanishing bits.
